Petrobras makes another oil discovery in Brazil's Foz do Amazonas basin
data.description:
Petrobras (PBR) said Friday it made another oil discovery in ultra-deep waters off Amapá state, strengthening indications of hydrocarbon potential along Brazil's Equatorial Margin.

The latest find follows a discovery in August, when Petrobras (PBR) first identified the presence of oil and natural gas at the Morpho exploration well in Block FZA-M-59 in the Foz do Amazonas Basin; the oil found in August was of good ​quality, the company said.

"The new discovery expands knowledge about the exploration potential of the area and will provide additional information for assessing the petroleum systems and resource potential of the Foz do Amazonas sedimentary basin," Petrobras (PBR) said.

The continued drilling of Morpho was aimed at evaluating deeper exploration intervals and led to this new discovery, the company added.

Petrobras (PBR) said recently it plans to ​drill three new wells ​in ⁠the area starting in January to determine the viability of commercial production in ​the environmentally-sensitive region.

data.title: iRhythm says June cyberattack accessed patient data
data.description:
• iRhythm Holdings (IRTC) said that an investigation into a June cybersecurity incident found that patient data, including name, contact information, date of birth, and insurance numbers, were accessed.
  • The company said it has begun notifying impacted impacted individuals.
  • iRhythm added that it has no evidence that the breach has led or will lead to identity theft.
  • The medical device technology firm reiterated that the incident did not impact its products, systems, or manufacturing and distribution operations, nor does it believe it will have a material impact on its financial results.

data.title: Most and least shorted utilities stocks with up to $2B market cap as of September end
data.description:
Within the utilities sector, short interest at the end of September was spread broadly across the sector, with no single industry emerging as a clear standout or dominating in terms of positioning.

Cadiz (CDZI)  recorded the highest short interest among utilities stocks with a market capitalization of up to $2B, with short interest at 11.28% of its shares outstanding, followed by Hawaiian Electric Industries (HE) at 10.88%, reflecting elevated bearish positioning in both stocks.

At the other end of the spectrum, Artesian Resources (ARTNA) and Hyflux (HYFXF) were among the least shorted utilities stocks, with short interest of 0.57% and 0.58%, respectively.

data.title: Gold futures turn lower as weak U.S. payrolls fail to sustain gains
data.description:
Gold futures ​fell on Friday, reversing earlier gains that followed a sharply weaker-than-expected U.S. employment report and succumbing to a continued selloff in U.S. Treasurys.

The Labor Department said just 29K jobs were created in September, well below expectations, after a downwardly revised increase of 133K in August.

The cooling in the labor market lowered the odds of another Federal Reserve rate hike at the end of October, sending gold higher, but Treasury yields rose as the day wore on, which pulled gold down; elevated yields tend to hurt the appeal of non-yielding bullion.

The benchmark 10-year yield fell in the morning to an intraday low of 5.155% before snapping back to 5.285%, near 2007 highs reached earlier this week.

The rise in yields came as oil prices bounced off early losses, keeping inflation concerns alive, as well as ongoing concerns about fast-rising borrowing by large AI corporations and ballooning government debt in Europe and the U.S.

Below the day-to-day movement, Deutsche Bank metals analyst Daniel Ghali pointed to gold's striking resilience in a high-rate environment, noting that official sector purchases are running at more than double their 2021 pace.

Ghali recently told BNN Bloomberg that the multi-decade highs in bond yields have pressured gold prices, but the metal still has not recorded a new low since July—"That's a really strong, resilient price action in my book," he said.

Gold's "weak performance in the context of the war in Iran has really shocked some participants, and has kept them on the sidelines," Ghali said. "But as we look forward to next year, we think this is a really strong setup. Positioning is low, gold is oversold as-is and it's underowned. So this is a really great time for gold."

Front-month Comex gold (XAUUSD:CUR) for October delivery dropped 0.9% to $4,133.70/oz, its lowest settlement value since August 4,  and front-month Comex October silver (XAGUSD:CUR) slipped 1.2% to $59.977/oz.

For the week, gold tumbled 3.6% and silver slid 6.7%, the fifth decline in the past six weeks for both metals.

data.title: FDA extends review for Novo Nordisk's denecimig for hemophilia A
data.description:
• The USA FDA has extended its review of Novo Nordisk's (NVO) BLA seeking approval of denecimig for hemophilia A.
  • The Danish pharma said that ongoing facility remediation activities at a manufacturing site for the drug are the reason for the delay.
  • Novo noted that the agency did not identify any issues with clinical trial data used to support its application.
  • Although the FDA didn't say when a decision on the BLA would come down, Novo said it is anticipating a US launch in H1 2027.

data.title: Western Digital retreats 10% amid storage selloff
data.description:
Western Digital (WDC) shares slumped just over 10% on Friday, with the stock falling $47.27 to close at $415.29.

The slide for the hard drive maker came along with a drop from peer Seagate Technology, as both succumbed to sector-level pressure. At the same time, flash-storage stock Sandisk dropped almost 4% and memory chipmaker Micron shed just over 2%.

data.title: Catheter Precision to rebrand as Flyte Aviation, adopt VJET ticker
data.description:
Catheter Precision (VTAK) announced Friday its board of directors has approved changing its name and ticker symbol to Flyte Aviation and "VJET," respectively.

Additionally, the company will effect a one-for-ten reverse stock split, as had been approved by stockholders at a special meeting of stockholders April 15, 2026.  

Every ten shares of common stock will be combined into one share, reducing the outstanding shares from approximately 21.0 million to approximately 2.1 million, with no change to the par value or authorized shares.

Shares will begin trading with the new name and ticker, on a split-adjusted basis, effective at the opening of trading on Monday, October 5, 2026.

Source: press release

data.title: AtlasClear approves multi-year stock option awards for executives and directors
data.description:
AtlasClear (ATCH) announced Friday that its compensation committee and board of directors approved long-term stock option awards for members of the company’s executive leadership team and Board of Directors.

The awards granted to the company’s board of directors consist of stock options to purchase 626,881 shares of the company’s common stock each, granted on October 1, 2026, at an exercise price of $0.2010 per share.

The firm added that the options vest in equal annual installments over three years, subject to continued service. The grants also include options to purchase 150,451 shares awarded to directors for service on the board of the company’s wholly owned subsidiary AtlasClearing. (155,451 for the chairman of the AtlasClearing board).

The company said it views stock options as an important part of its strategy to attract, retain, and motivate experienced executives and directors as the company continues to develop and expand its financial services platform. 

Source: press release

data.title: Intermex, Western Union file premerger notification with the FTC
data.description:
International Money Express (IMXI) and Western Union (WU) filed a premerger notification with the FTC and DOJ regarding the deal.

The parties filed on Friday, as the HSR clearance was set to expire on Tuesday, as clearance under the HSR ACT only lasts a year, according to an 8-K filing on Friday. Based on talks with California's DFPI, the parties don't expect the regulator to reinstate its approval before Tuesday.

The filing starts a new 30-day waiting period under the HSR Act, and the companies have requested early termination of the waiting period. Intermex (IMXI) and Western Union (WU) continue to engage in talks with the DFPI regarding the reinstatement of the regulator's approval. 

In August, the companies announced that they received a letter from the California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation suspending the approval extension previously granted on July 31. 

Western Union (WU) agreed to buy Intermex for $16/share in cash last August.
